papers.title: MR-MAS: An End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Mendelian Randomization Analysis
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Understanding disease-related causal mechanisms is essential for biomedical research, yet the practical use of Mendelian Randomization (MR) remains constrained by fragmented analytical workflows and a strong dependence on specialized expertise. These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses. Results We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. Additional evaluations showed robust trait retrieval and improved code-repair performance with MRKB guidance. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research. Availability and Implementation The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS , with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636

MOTIVATION: Understanding disease-related causal mechanisms is essential for biomedical research, yet the practical use of Mendelian Randomization (MR) remains constrained by fragmented analytical workflows and a strong dependence on specialized expertise. These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses.

RESULTS: We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. Additional evaluations showed robust trait retrieval and improved code-repair performance with MRKB guidance. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS, with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
理解与疾病相关的因果机制是生物医学研究的核心任务，然而孟德尔随机化分析的实际应用仍受到分散的分析流程及对专业知识的高度依赖的限制。这些因素阻碍了高效、标准化且可重复的端到端分析过程的实施。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了MR-MAS这一基于多智能体架构的自动化孟德尔随机化分析系统。该系统充分利用大型语言模型的推理与协调能力，并整合外部工具，将数据采集、因果效应估计、结果解读及论文撰写等环节纳入统一的处理流程，从而显著降低人工干预的需求。此外，MR-MAS还配备了结构化的孟德尔随机化知识库，为方法的应用与分析代码的优化提供了有力支持。在多种测试场景中，MR-MAS均展现了稳定的运行效率，成功再现了多项文献中验证过的因果关系，并能在重复实验或使用不同模型时保持结果的一致性。进一步评估表明，在该知识库的辅助下，系统的特征提取能力得到提升，代码修复效果也更为显著。这些结果表明，MR-MAS确实能为生物医学研究中的大规模、标准化及可重复的分析工作提供有力支持。  

**开源与实施信息**  
源代码、孟德尔随机化知识库以及相关基准数据均可在以下链接免费获取：https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS。本研究所使用的版本存档地址为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636

all_papers.title: MR-MAS: An End-to-End Multi-Agent System for Autonomous Mendelian Randomization Analysis
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Understanding disease-related causal mechanisms is essential for biomedical research, yet the practical use of Mendelian Randomization (MR) remains constrained by fragmented analytical workflows and a strong dependence on specialized expertise. These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses. Results We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. Additional evaluations showed robust trait retrieval and improved code-repair performance with MRKB guidance. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research. Availability and Implementation The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS , with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636

These challenges limit the efficient, standardized, and reproducible execution of end-to-end MR analyses.

RESULTS: We propose MR-MAS, an end-to-end automated MR analysis system built on a multi-agent architecture. MR-MAS leverages the reasoning and coordination capabilities of large language models (LLMs) and integrates external tools to unify data acquisition, causal effect estimation, results interpretation, and manuscript preparation into a single workflow, thereby reducing manual effort. MR-MAS further incorporates a structured Mendelian Randomization Knowledge Base (MRKB) to support MR method implementation and targeted repair of MR analysis code. Across diverse test scenarios, MR-MAS demonstrated stable workflow execution, reproduced several literature-supported causal signals, and maintained consistent causal estimates across repeated runs and different model backends. These results suggest that MR-MAS may provide practical support for scalable, standardized, and reproducible MR analyses in biomedical research.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The source code, MRKB, and benchmark data are freely available at https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS, with the version used in this study archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636.

MR-MAS利用大型语言模型的推理与协调能力，并整合外部工具，将数据采集、因果效应分析、结果解读以及论文撰写等流程统一到一个工作体系中，从而显著减少人工操作的工作量。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
理解与疾病相关的因果机制是生物医学研究的核心任务，然而孟德尔随机化分析的实际应用仍受到分散的分析流程及对专业知识的高度依赖的限制。这些因素阻碍了高效、标准化且可重复的端到端分析过程的实施。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了MR-MAS这一基于多智能体架构的自动化孟德尔随机化分析系统。该系统充分利用大型语言模型的推理与协调能力，并整合外部工具，将数据采集、因果效应估计、结果解读及论文撰写等环节纳入统一的处理流程，从而显著降低人工干预的需求。此外，MR-MAS还配备了结构化的孟德尔随机化知识库，为方法的应用与分析代码的优化提供了有力支持。在多种测试场景中，MR-MAS均展现了稳定的运行效率，成功再现了多项文献中验证过的因果关系，并能在重复实验或使用不同模型时保持结果的一致性。进一步评估表明，在该知识库的辅助下，系统的特征提取能力得到提升，代码修复效果也更为显著。这些结果表明，MR-MAS确实能为生物医学研究中的大规模、标准化及可重复的分析工作提供有力支持。  

**开源与实施信息**  
源代码、孟德尔随机化知识库以及相关基准数据均可在以下链接免费获取：https://github.com/Zaiwen/MR-MAS。本研究所使用的版本存档地址为：https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20342636

all_papers.title: A distinct serological signature of preterm birth
all_papers.summary: Preterm birth is the leading cause of death in children globally. We determined proteome-wide autoantibody profiles for 2,195 pregnant individuals, revealing a shared humoral program of normal pregnancy and a distinct, expanded autoreactive signature that precedes preterm birth
all_papers.llm_title_zh: 早产特有的血清学特征
all_papers.llm_title_bilingual: 早产特有的血清学特征 / A distinct serological signature of preterm birth
all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 早产是全球儿童死亡的主要原因。
llm_highlights_zh: 我们对2,195名孕妇进行了全蛋白质组水平的自身抗体检测，结果发现：正常妊娠过程中存在一种共同的体液免疫反应模式，而那些在早产前出现症状的孕妇则表现出一种明显增强的自身免疫反应特征。
早产特有的血清学特征
早产是全球儿童死亡的主要原因。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 早产是全球儿童死亡的主要原因。我们对2,195名孕妇进行了全蛋白质组水平的自身抗体检测，结果发现：正常妊娠过程中存在某些共同的体液免疫反应特征，而而在早产发生之前，这些特征会发生变化，出现一种独特且扩增的自身免疫反应模式。
